chapter_theme: A song at Sivapuram (சிவபுரம்): the poet asks that his mind, wandering in the joys and sorrows of a body made of the elements, be conquered and joined to grace on the path of supreme knowledge; the praise is a litany of Parvati and the Man-Lion as Murugan's uncle.

872.reading: The poet speaks of the one body made of mind and the five elements, in which he wanders in pleasure, sorrow and desire, and asks Murugan to conquer that mind and join him, a dog of a servant, to grace so that he gains the good path of supreme knowledge. The praise calls Murugan the son of Parvati, named as Janani, Sankari, Narani, the spotless one full of the eight qualities, the cause, Siva's consort; the vel that freed the imprisoned gods and uprooted the asuras; the nephew of Vishnu who came as the Man-Lion from the pillar Hiranya struck and drank his blood; and the lord praised by gods and sages at Sivapuram, whose houses are filled with gold by the eight Lakshmis.
872.nuance: மனமெனும் பொருள் ... கூடியதோர் உடல்: mind is counted with sky, wind, fire, water and earth as what makes up the body, and the plea is to conquer the mind (மதியை வென்று), not the body. பதி மூணெழு வகையாலே is obscure; it may count kinds of birth or constituents. The Narasimha story is told in its detail (the pillar, the claws, the blood drunk like nectar), more fully than usual. திருமடந்தையர் நாலிருவோர் are the eight Lakshmis.
